draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Ottapalam! This town on the Bharathapuzha, Kerala's second-longest river, is one of the state's big filming locations. The 2010 film Pokkiri Raja was shot here.
draft.hungryLine: Ottapalam has plenty of simple local restaurants. Try Sadhya Restaurant on Market line or Kayyalakkal Restaurant on Ali Akbar Road.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Vengeri Temple is a 6 min walk and Puzhikunnu Temple about 8 min. Chinakathoor Kavu Temple is the one to see at festival time.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk down to the banks of the Bharathapuzha and watch the river go by.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Ottapalam used to be called Ayirur Thekkummuri Desam.

legends.title: A Pooram every year
legends.body: The Chinakathoor Pooram festival is held at this temple every year. At Sri Chinnakkathoor Bhagavathy Temple in Lakkidi, the famous festival runs 21 days, with costumes and animal shapes on show.

legends.title: A first for Kerala
legends.body: Chunangad, a village near Ottapalam, is where Chunangat Kunjikavamma was born. She became the first woman President of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee.

tips.title: Time it for Pooram.
tips.body: Chinakathoor Pooram happens every year, so check the dates locally before you come.

tips.title: Dress modestly at temples.
tips.body: Most sights within walking distance are temples, so cover shoulders and knees.

story.title: The Nedunganad kingdom
story.body: Ottapalam, Pattambi and Cherpulassery were part of the Nedunganad kingdom, led by the Nedunganathiripad. Its headquarters was at Makovilakam near Kodikunnu.

story.title: Land of Thrikkadeeri Nair
story.body: Nair chiefs ruled under the Nedunganathiripad, and Ottapalam was the administrative area of Thrikkadeeri Nair. Back then it was known as Ayirur Thekkummuri Desam.

story.title: A seat of its own
story.body: Ottapalam had its own Lok Sabha constituency, reserved for scheduled castes. In 2009 it was replaced by the Alathur constituency.

story.title: Lights, camera, Ottapalam
story.body: It's the taluk headquarters and one of the district's main commercial centres. Film crews love it, and the 2010 film Pokkiri Raja was shot here.
